title: An unsigned cipher letter to Lorenzo de' Medici from the court of Castile, Toledo, 31 August 1479 (ASF, MAP LXXII 171): a letter cipher read in part by Prabal Gupta

documents.shelfmark: Archivio di Stato di Firenze, Mediceo avanti il Principato, filza LXXII, doc. 171 (old c. 203)
documents.date: 31 August 1479 (note on the verso; the recto ends 'In Toledo')
documents.route: an unnamed writer at the court of Castile (Toledo) -> Lorenzo de' Medici, Florence

plaintext.source: The printed MAP inventory lists the letter as 'Anonimo. (De Spagna, 1479 ago. 31)' with no content; the contributor found no clear copy, key or decipherment.

transcription.source: the contributor's transcription of the archive's images by AI models, every doubtful sign re-read against the images; the project did not see the images and no human has checked
transcription.notes: Images served at 1,272 by 1,848 pixels, so cipher signs are 8 to 14 pixels high; clear text in brackets is provisional.

system.summary: One sign per letter (20 signs, two for h) with word division kept, clear words between the cipher runs, and about 60 code numbers and nomenclator symbols for persons and other words that stay unread.

prior_solution.where: The printed MAP inventory (vol. III, 1957, p. 183) gives no content; the contributor searched the ledger and the web and found no reading. Rubinstein's edition of Lorenzo's letters and studies of Florentines in Castile were not checked.

conditions.human_role: Prabal Gupta set the task and directed the work (issue #332, repository prabal-rje/branicki-1757); AI models transcribed the images, fitted the key on the clear words between the cipher runs and read the result; a second AI model reviewed the readings. The project re-ran the decryption and a shuffled-key control; it has not seen the images.

solution.what: AI models transcribed the signs of the letter from the archive's images (1,272 by 1,848 pixels) and re-read every doubtful sign against the images; no human check.
A letter key was fitted on an Italian letter model with the clear words between the cipher runs as cribs; 20 signs valued.
The decryption was read as 15th-century Italian: 88 of 113 cipher words read in full, 21 doubtful and 4 open; about 60 code items stay unread; an independent AI review applied.

Contributor's controls: a word-list test (65.3% of letter positions in listed words against a mean of 1.9% and a best of 11.4% for 200 shuffled keys), a blind check of 31 words (30 agreed) and a method check on test texts (98.5% to 99.8%).
The contributor searched the printed MAP inventory, the ledger and the web: no reading found; Rubinstein's edition and studies of Florentines in Castile were not checked.

Project check: an own script applied key.tsv to the 108 cipher words that are runs of letter signs and got the contributor's literal decodes in all 108; a word-list test gives 55.1% of letters in listed words against a mean of 9.4% and a best of 27.7% for 200 shuffled keys (VERIFICATION.md). No image compared.

validation.notes: The project's n-gram test needs a 15th-century Italian model and the cipher text is short; a word-list test against 200 shuffled keys was used instead (VERIFICATION.md).

outcome.method_basis: Contributor's claim: the key was found from the cipher of this letter alone, with the clear words between the cipher runs as cribs and no key sheet; the project verified that the key decrypts the cipher words into Italian and re-ran a shuffled-key control, but did not repeat the search or see the images.

texts.label: Cipher letter 'De Spagna' to Lorenzo de' Medici, Toledo, 31 August 1479 (ASF, MAP LXXII 171)
texts.summary: An unsigned letter from the court of Castile to Lorenzo de' Medici, in the contributor's reading: the writer's last letter went through a merchant's house at Seville; a league 'a difensione degli stati' has been or will be concluded; the parties show 'sì poca fermeza'; someone is devoted to Lorenzo ('ve ne potete fidare') and a brother of his is the comendador mayor of Alcántara and the writer's close friend; an agreement with the queen is to be made; a betrothal, a legate, a tithe on the clergy of which one party 'tocha la metà'. Persons are code items and stay unread; the context (the peace of Alcáçovas, 4 September 1479) is the contributor's inference.

reading_review.note: Read the contributor's Italian and English as clauses: single sentences build, but most lines carry holes at the code items and doubtful signs, and the clear hand between the cipher runs is provisional; no sentence of the cipher is whole.
